paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Japan
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the distribution of polarity scores for vaccine-related sentiments in Japan, with the x-axis representing polarity scores ranging from -1.0 to 0.6 on a linear scale, marked at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis shows the corresponding counts, ranging from 0 to 40,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 10,000. A single blue line with circular markers connects data points, showing the frequency of each polarity score. The counts are relatively low and nearly flat from -1.0 to -0.6, with values around 1,000 to 2,000. From -0.6 to -0.2, the counts gradually increase to approximately 13,000. There is a sharp rise to a peak of 40,000 at a polarity score of 0.0. Following this, the counts drop to about 8,000 at 0.2, then rise again to around 25,000 at 0.2, before decreasing to approximately 13,000 at 0.4 and dropping to about 2,000 at 0.6. The overall trend indicates a strong concentration of sentiments around neutral polarity (0.0), with fewer negative and positive sentiments.
